endorsements.quote: A qualified subject matter expert must review the artifact for factual accuracy, clinical safety, guideline consistency, and unacceptable omissions.
Therefore, an accountable human reviewer must be explicitly linked to the artifact from generation to final approval.
To preserve transparency, the workflow must record the AI provenance of the artifact, including the tool used, the nature of the prompt, and the human reviewer responsible for the final decision.

The gate requires that the range be fixed in advance with its rationale and that items outside it be recorded rather than silently retained.
A proportion of artifacts, fixed in advance, is rated independently by two reviewers blinded to each other's decision.
Every coefficient is reported with a 95% confidence interval.
Only an item whose empirical results have been reviewed and accepted at this second passage may proceed to approval for scored use.

unlisted_practices: Classify each AI-generated assessment artifact by type and intended use before evaluation, since different artifact families carry different validation burdens.
Review AI-generated test items against established item-writing guidelines for cueing, ambiguity, non-functioning distractors, and construct-irrelevant language.
Map each AI-generated assessment item to a curriculum, competency, or exam blueprint and do not use items that cannot be defensibly mapped.

Document a plan for empirical psychometric evaluation (pilot testing, item difficulty and discrimination, distractor analysis, DIF review) before any AI-generated item is used for scored or consequential assessment.
Perform differential item functioning review when assessment scores affect comparisons across learner groups, and follow flagged items with content review.

Measure inter-rater reproducibility of expert review gates using independent blinded ratings before adjudication, with prespecified minimum agreement that halts the process for recalibration if unmet.
Treat AI-generated assessment materials as preliminary candidates requiring staged review rather than ready-made instruments.

screen.reason: Technical report presenting a governance framework/workflow (staged human-governed validation) for evaluating AI-generated medical assessment artifacts rather than an empirical evaluation.
